problem: A bag contains $9$ different colored marbles. Jamie takes $4$ marbles from the bag, one at a time, and puts them in the order they were taken from the bag to create a sequence of colors. How many different sequences of colors are possible?

feedback.problem: Of the $7$ students who are going to take a test, the top $2$ will get different prizes. In how many ways can both prizes be awarded?
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $7$ students, so $n=7.$ We want to select $2$ of those students for both the prizes, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the prizes is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{7}{P}_{2} & =\frac{7!}{(7-2)!} \\  & =\frac{7!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =7\cdot 6 \\  & =42.\end{aligned}
$$
